correctness.rationale: Norm N10=max{|u+v|,|ru+v|,r|v|,r|u|,|u+rv|}, r=(sqrt5-1)/2; real plane. The described ten polygon vertices satisfy its support inequalities and the displayed Q,R generate the needed dihedral symmetry to reduce x to one half-edge (alpha in [0,1/2]) and y to five antipodal edge classes. For each edge y=p+beta(q-p) and t in either [0,r] or [r,1], substitute w=t beta, yielding affine support values in alpha,t,w on a triangular prism. Candidate upper envelope L(t)=1+(sqrt5-1)t/4 and (1+sqrt5)/4+r t. Failure of upper bound requires a pair of 10 signed linear supports simultaneously above L; the maximum of their minimum over a prism is attained at an original vertex or equality-plane intersection with an edge (possibly a face degeneration covered by a vertex). Inspected exact Q(sqrt5) verifier constructs all eight prism vertices, every equality/facet/facet candidate, and evaluates 5*2*10*10=1000 cases exactly; tabulated maxima low=(0,0,0,0,0), high=((-9+3sqrt5)/4,(-3+sqrt5)/4,0,0,(-3+sqrt5)/2), all <=0. Independently solved same 1000 small linear max-min programs numerically; agrees to double precision (not substituted for exact proof). At both branch endpoints, unit pairs (-1,0),((3+sqrt5)/4,-(1+sqrt5)/2) and (-1/2,-1/2),(phi,-phi), phi=(1+sqrt5)/2, attain branch norms, and convexity/support affinity extends their exact equalities throughout. Homogeneity J(lambda)=s F((1-s)/s), s=max(lambda,1-lambda), yields two stated weighted branches and threshold s=r, for 0<lambda<1. Midpoint ordinary J is a derived known value, not the new claim.

value.rationale: The regular/affine-regular decagon is a canonical new shape in polygonal Banach geometry, and the full weighted generalized James invariant is a natural continuum geometric profile. A verified nontrivial golden-ratio transition of the sharp extremizer and complete exact formula are stronger than a known midpoint value and require a substantive sharp continuous polyhedral bound. This is a motivated exact classification, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice or a trivial parameter rename; the distinct phase of optimal pairs may inform norm geometry examples and comparison work.
